data.name: Kanya
data.long_meaning: Kanya refers to a virgin or unmarried girl in Hindu culture and mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kanyā’, meaning ‘girl’ or ‘young woman’. In Hindu mythology, Kanya represents the goddess Durga in her virgin form.

historical_references.reference: Kanya was an alternate name for the goddess Durga in her form as the virgin goddess, often depicted with seven heads and twelve arms.
historical_references.context: Durga Puja, an important Hindu festival, celebrates Durga's victory over the demon Mahishasura.

historical_references.reference: In Hindu mythology, Kanya is also the name of the constellation Virgo, personified as the goddess of fertility, agriculture, and harvest.
historical_references.context: Vedic texts and astronomical records describe the constellation as a female deity, associated with the god Indra.
